raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #40564

## Motivation

`MooncakeHostTensorAllocator.allocate` feeds the raw return value of
`MooncakeHostMemAllocator.alloc(size)` into `ctypes.from_address` and
`torch.frombuffer` without checking it. When the underlying allocator cannot map the
host segment it returns a null pointer, and both of those happily accept address 0, so
`allocate()` returns a normal-looking tensor whose `data_ptr()` is `0`.

Nothing fails where the allocation actually failed. The error surfaces much later and
far from its cause: pinning the host pool calls `cudaHostRegister` on address 0 and
gets `cudaErrorInvalidValue`, or the process segfaults on the first access to the
buffer. Neither message mentions host memory, so in a prefill deployment we spent a
long detour on the CUDA side before identifying the host memory shortage as the real
problem.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py`: check
  `ptr_int` right after `self.allocator.alloc(size)` and raise a `RuntimeError` naming
  the requested size in both bytes and GB, pointing at host memory availability and
  the mooncake allocator logs. Nothing else in the allocation path changes; a
  successful allocation behaves exactly as before.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_host_allocator.py`: new CPU unit test.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — this is a pure error path, and a successful allocation is untouched,
so no model output changes.

A CPU unit test covers the new behaviour. It bypasses `__init__` with `__new__` (so it
needs neither a mooncake install nor a mappable host segment) and mocks the underlying
allocator into returning `0` and `None`, asserting that `allocate()` raises a
`RuntimeError` whose message carries the requested size:

```
$ python -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_host_allocator.py -q
1 passed, 2 subtests passed in 4.36s
```

The existing mooncake unit tests in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`
(`test_mooncake_ssd_offload_path.py`, `test_mooncake_store_config.py`,
`test_mooncake_tenant_config.py`, `test_mooncake_group_semantics.py`,
`test_mooncake_standalone_dummy_mamba.py`) still pass: 32 passed before the change,
33 passed with the new test added.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The added check is a single truthiness test on an integer that runs
once per host pool allocation, and it only changes behaviour on the failure path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing documentation change)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (error path only, no accuracy or speed impact)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Thanks for the rerun! On attempt 2 the previously failing `base-b-test-1-gpu-large (0)` passed, along with the other base-b jobs that ran. The required `pr-test-finish` is red only because five H100 jobs (`base-b-test-1-gpu-large (1)(2)(3)`, `base-b-test-2-gpu-large (3)(4)`) were still queued after ~4 hours and got cancelled at ~10:45 UTC, together with many other PRs' runs. There are no test failures. @huangtingwei9988 could you please `/rerun-failed-ci` once more? Thanks!

Thanks again for the rerun! Attempt 3 got through all base-b jobs. The only real failure is in base-c: `base-c-test-4-gpu-b200 (0)` → `test_glm53_flash_b200.py::TestGLM53FlashB200LowLatency.test_gsm8k` scored 0.928 against a 0.93 threshold. This looks like accuracy noise near the threshold rather than something caused by this PR:

- The same job failed the same way on another PR's run (38112419109, GLM-5.3-Flash gsm8k 0.918–0.926), and passed on the other 35 PR runs I checked from 10-08 to 10-12.
- This PR only adds a null-pointer check in the Mooncake host allocator and a CPU unit test; the GLM-5.3-Flash test does not use that code.
- The other nine base-c failures are fail-fast skips that never ran tests.

@huangtingwei9988 could you please `/rerun-failed-ci` once more? If you can, adding the `bypass-fail-fast` label first would let the rest of base-c finish in the same attempt, even if this test misses the threshold again. If it keeps failing only on this known-flaky test, would merging despite it be an option? Thanks!

detail.title: [HiCache] Fail fast on a null pointer from the Mooncake host allocator

files.patch:
@@ -53,6 +53,13 @@ def allocate(
             size *= d
         size *= torch.tensor([], dtype=self.dtype).element_size()
         ptr_int = self.allocator.alloc(size)
+        if not ptr_int:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"MooncakeHostMemAllocator.alloc returned a null pointer for "
+                f"{size / 1024**3:.3f} GB ({size} bytes); the mooncake host memory "
+                f"allocator could not map the segment (check host memory "
+                f"availability and the mooncake allocator logs)."
+            )
         self.ptr = ptr_int
         c_type = ctypes.c_byte * size
         c_array = c_type.from_address(ptr_int)

@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@
+"""Unit tests for MooncakeHostTensorAllocator allocation failures."""
+
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.storage.mooncake_store.mooncake_store import (
+    MooncakeHostTensorAllocator,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestMooncakeHostTensorAllocator(CustomTestCase):
+    def _make_allocator(self, alloc_return):
+        # Bypass __init__: it constructs the real MooncakeHostMemAllocator,
+        # which requires the mooncake package and a mappable host segment.
+        allocator = MooncakeHostTensorAllocator.__new__(MooncakeHostTensorAllocator)
+        allocator.allocator = mock.Mock(alloc=mock.Mock(return_value=alloc_return))
+        allocator.ptr = None
+        return allocator
+
+    def test_null_pointer_from_allocator_raises(self):
+        for alloc_return in (0, None):
+            with self.subTest(alloc_return=alloc_return):
+                allocator = self._make_allocator(alloc_return)
+
+                with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError) as ctx:
+                    allocator.allocate((1024, 1024), dtype=torch.uint8)
+
+                message = str(ctx.exception)
+                self.assertIn("1048576 bytes", message)
+                self.assertIn("0.001 GB", message)
+                self.assertIn("mooncake host memory", message)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
